back: Metals that contain iron. They are magnetic and rust, so need a protective finish.
Metals that do not contain iron. They are not magnetic and do not rust.
Low carbon steel (0.15–0.35% carbon). Ductile, tough and easy to braze and weld, but corrodes easily — nuts and bolts, bicycle frames, car parts.
0.35–0.7% carbon. Stronger and harder than mild steel but less ductile; can be hardened and tempered — garden tools, springs, hammer heads.
Tool steel (0.7–1.4% carbon). Hard but brittle — tools, screwdrivers and chisels.

front: Effect of carbon content on steel
back: More carbon makes steel harder but more brittle.
Strong in compression but brittle if thin, with poor corrosion resistance — gates, manhole covers, vices.
Lightweight, malleable, strong and a good conductor — drinks cans, cycle frames, saucepans. Melts at about 660°C.
Very malleable, excellent conductor of heat and electricity, oxidises green — plumbing and electrical wiring.
A mixture of metals, or a metal with another element, to improve working properties or aesthetics.
Copper + zinc. Golden, strong and ductile — taps, door fittings, hinges, musical instruments.
Copper + tin. Hard, corrosion resistant, low friction — bearings, monuments and nautical parts.
Iron + chromium + nickel. Hard, tough and resists stains and corrosion — sinks, cutlery, hospital equipment.
Mainly tin with small amounts of copper and antimony. Melts at about 170–230°C, so ideal for casting in school.

front: Why is pewter cast in MDF moulds?
back: MDF resists the heat, is easy to cut and has no grain.
Burns from molten metal (gloves, leather apron, face shield); moisture making metal spit (keep everything dry); fumes (ventilation); spills (pour over a sand tray).
A metal's ability to withstand friction and abrasion.
How well a metal resists fracturing when a force is applied.
The ability to bend or stretch under a force and return to the original shape when the force is removed.
The ability to be permanently changed in shape without cracking, keeping the new shape once the force is removed.
The ability to be drawn or deformed without fracture.
The ability to be bent or shaped easily.
